skills/toil/github.md

Pull requests, reviews, comments, checks, labels, assignees and issues on GitHub.com and GitHub Enterprise Server, through the REST API and, for review threads, PR status, auto-merge, the merge queue and drafts, the GraphQL API. The two differ only in host, so they’re one area with a configurable baseUrl. Verification level: unit.

Supported versions: The oldest GitHub Enterprise Server version toil supports hasn’t been established. toil pins REST API version 2022-11-28 and uses GraphQL for review threads, PR status, auto-merge, the merge queue and drafts. GitHub.com is always current; no Enterprise Server release has been verified yet, and the auto-merge and merge-queue commands need a release that has those features.

Credential

A fine-grained personal access token: Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens → Fine-grained tokens, with access to the repositories you work on (pull requests, issues, contents and checks, read or write as needed). toil sends it as Authorization: Bearer <token>, with Accept: application/vnd.github+json and X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2022-11-28. There is no OAuth app, username, password or browser login.

Configuration

KeyEnv varRequiredMeaning
baseUrlTOIL_GITHUB_BASE_URL, then GITHUB_API_URLyesThe REST API root: https://api.github.com, or https://ghe.imagile.dev/api/v3 for Enterprise Server
tokenTOIL_GITHUB_TOKEN, then GITHUB_TOKENyesFine-grained personal access token
ownerTOIL_GITHUB_OWNERnoDefault owner (user or org)
repoTOIL_GITHUB_REPOnoDefault repository name
targetBranchTOIL_GITHUB_TARGET_BRANCHnoDefault base branch for create-pr (main when unset)
writesTOIL_GITHUB_WRITESnotrue lets write commands run (with --allow-write)

CI fallbacks: in GitHub Actions, the default connection takes its token from GITHUB_TOKEN when TOIL_GITHUB_TOKEN isn’t set, and its base URL from GITHUB_API_URL when TOIL_GITHUB_BASE_URL isn’t set. Each sits directly below its TOIL_GITHUB_* variable and above the config file.

The GraphQL endpoint is derived from baseUrl: a trailing /v3 is dropped and /graphql appended, so https://api.github.com uses https://api.github.com/graphql and https://ghe.imagile.dev/api/v3 uses https://ghe.imagile.dev/api/graphql.

Environment variables (CI, or a one-off shell):

export TOIL_GITHUB_BASE_URL=https://ghe.imagile.dev/api/v3
export TOIL_GITHUB_TOKEN=<your fine-grained token>

Or ~/.toil/config.json, with owner, repo and targetBranch usually set once under defaults.github:

{
  "version": 2,
  "connections": {
    "corp-github": { "area": "github", "baseUrl": "https://ghe.imagile.dev/api/v3" }
  },
  "defaults": { "github": { "connection": "corp-github", "owner": "imagile", "repo": "toil-probe" } }
}

The token never goes in this file; a plaintext one there is refused with CONFIG_INVALID. Run toil connections add corp-github --area github (or toil connections login corp-github for an existing connection) to keep it in the OS credential store, or set TOIL_GITHUB_TOKEN.

Owner and repository

Every command except create-repo needs an owner and a repository, which come from, in order:

  1. --owner and --repo, before or after the command (toil github --owner imagile --repo toil-probe get-pr --number 7); on create-pr the ones after the command win
  2. the first of the working folder’s remotes whose host is this connection’s host, of any name, trying origin first (so a fork’s upstream counts) (api.github.com counts as github.com). git@host:o/r, ssh://git@host[:port]/o/r and https://host[:port]/o/r remotes are read, each with or without .git; an HTTPS remote with a user name in it isn’t
  3. the connection’s owner and repo (usually defaults.github)

With neither found, the command fails with “Could not determine GitHub owner/repo”. resolve-thread needs them too, though it acts by thread id alone. create-repo reads only an explicit --owner, always as an organization (POST /orgs/<owner>/repos); without it the repository is created under the token’s user.

Commands

Numbers (--number, --comment-id, --line) are read as whole numbers from the start of the text, so 12abc is 12. Write commands need writes on the connection and --allow-write. The deletes (delete-comment, delete-review-comment, remove-label, remove-reviewers, remove-assignees) run on the CLI only and are never MCP tools. Owner, repo, labels and refs go into request paths as typed; a value that would make a . or .. path segment is refused with INVALID_INPUT.

  • Repositories and issues: create-repo (--name, --description, --private, --auto-init); create-issue (--title, --body or --body-file <path> with - for stdin, repeatable --label and --assignee).
  • Pull requests: list-prs (--state open|closed|all, default open; --head user:branch, --base; --author and --created-after/--created-before, ISO 8601, are filtered after every page is in, the author case-insensitively; a date alone is UTC midnight, a date-time with no zone local time), get-pr, create-pr (--title, --head, --base defaulting to targetBranch then main, --body/--body-file, --draft), update-pr (--title, --body, --base), merge-pr (--method merge|squash|rebase, default merge, always sent; --commit-title, --commit-message), close-pr, reopen-pr, convert-to-draft, ready-for-review.
  • Merging: enable-auto-merge and enqueue-pr (--method, --match-head-commit <sha>), disable-auto-merge.
  • Comments: list-comments, add-comment, list-review-comments, add-inline-comment (--commit, --file, --line, --side LEFT|RIGHT, default RIGHT), reply-comment (--comment-id), delete-comment, delete-review-comment.
  • Diff and files: diff returns { diff }, the unified diff as text; list-files.
  • Reviews: list-reviews, approve (--body optional), request-changes (--body required), list-reviewers, list-review-threads (thread ids for resolve-thread; the first 100 threads with a GITHUB_REVIEW_THREADS_TRUNCATED warning past that, and the first 10 comments of each), resolve-thread --thread-id, add-reviewers and remove-reviewers (repeatable --reviewer and --team-reviewer, at least one).
  • Status: get-status --ref (the combined status; GitHub’s first 30 statuses), list-checks --ref, pr-status (review decision, mergeability, draft and auto-merge state, and the first 100 checks counted into checks.passed, failed, pending and other).
  • Labels and assignees: add-labels (repeatable --label), remove-label --label, add-assignees and remove-assignees (repeatable --assignee).

Lists page 100 at a time until a short page, and stop with an error after 1,000 pages.

toil github list-prs --state all --author octo-dev
toil github --owner imagile --repo toil-probe pr-status --number 7
toil github create-pr --title "Add the probe" --head feature --body-file pr.md --allow-write

Checking a dossier

check-dossier checks the call’s dossier: each owner it names (owner, per repo or not, and owners) is a user or organization, and each repository (repo) exists under its owner. It’s toil github check-dossier (--dossier <name|file>, or the dossier the folder resolves to), and it returns { dossier, connection, env, ok, checked, checks, unchecked }, one check per value with its key path. The CLI exits 1 when one is missing. A failure other than not-found (a bad token, an unreachable host) fails the command. Read only.

Settings at a glance

  • baseUrl required

    REST API root: https://api.github.com, or https://ghe.imagile.dev/api/v3 for Enterprise Server

    TOIL_GITHUB_BASE_URL orGITHUB_API_URL

  • token required secret

    Fine-grained personal access token

    TOIL_GITHUB_TOKEN orGITHUB_TOKEN

  • owner

    Default owner (user or org)

    TOIL_GITHUB_OWNER

  • repo

    Default repository name

    TOIL_GITHUB_REPO

  • targetBranch

    Default base branch for create-pr (main when unset)

    TOIL_GITHUB_TARGET_BRANCH
